quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from what parts of your vehicle?

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You need to see clearly through all your vehicle's windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors.

questions.question: Which lane should you use to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: Keep wheels straight while waiting to turn left. On a hill or slope, turn your wheels so your vehicle won't roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Where should you start a left turn from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start from the far left lane.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Breathe in fresh air.
Give your body time.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol leaves your system slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. Only time will lower it.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must always carry proof of insurance. Show it to a police officer after any traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front moves right to let you pass.
When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
When the yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
The lane must turn right.
You can only turn right on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming road conditions like curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same traffic rules.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car.
Motorcycles brake more slowly than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. Following too closely puts both you and the motorcyclist at risk. You need space and time to avoid a crash.

questions.question: When you see an octagonal sign, you must:

options.text: Slow down.
Stop.
Turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means Stop. Come to a complete stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians with the right-of-way. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing you.
Cars coming toward you.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming cars going straight. You can only turn when it is safe and does not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is a major cause of traffic crashes. Distractions cause drivers to miss important sights and sounds that help prevent crashes.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and wait until the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and look carefully before going through. You do not have to stop completely.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a downhill curve. You should:

options.text: Slow down before entering the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead. Braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to traffic that could cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lanes you want to enter. Be ready to stop if there is traffic. You may go through without stopping if no traffic is coming.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no passing is allowed in either direction. You cannot cross the centerline to pass.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely when:

options.text: All vehicles are going about the same speed.
One lane is going faster than other lanes.
One vehicle is going faster or slower than the traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is going faster or slower than the traffic flow.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other traffic. Speeding increases crash risk. Going too slowly also raises the risk of rear-end collisions and causes other drivers to swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: This symbol is used for:

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: An orange reflective triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves at slow speeds. You may see this on farm equipment, work vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It looks like a solid orange triangle during the day and a hollow red triangle at night.

questions.question: What should a driver do?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules help drivers know who should go first. But no driver should assume they automatically have the right-of-way. Always look at what is happening at the intersection. If giving up the right-of-way prevents a crash, do it.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop before crossing the intersection.
Slow down and go through carefully.
Wait for a green light before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go through carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down. Check for traffic coming from other directions. Then proceed with care.

questions.question: You are entering an interstate highway. You should:

options.text: Find a safe space and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe space and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, find a gap that is large enough to enter the traffic safely. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: Pentagon signs warn you that you are near or entering a school zone or school crossing. Watch for children. Follow the posted speed limits.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the other vehicle.
Pass as safely and quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly so you can see the road ahead clearly. Move back to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
